title: Alternator Not Charging
summary: Charging-system workflow for low alternator output, battery light, belt drive issues, and voltage-drop faults.
intro: An alternator-not-charging complaint should be diagnosed with a known-good battery state, belt-drive inspection, charging output under load, and voltage-drop checks before replacing the alternator.
common_sounds: Headlights dim at idle or blower slows down
Belt squeal, pulley noise, or burning smell
quick_checks: Charge and test the battery before judging alternator output
Measure charging voltage at idle and raised RPM with electrical loads on
Inspect belt, tensioner, pulley alignment, alternator clutch pulley, and output cable
Voltage-drop alternator B+, battery positive, grounds, and engine ground strap under load
Check generator command, sense wire, fuses, and related P0562/P0620 data
common_causes: Failed alternator or internal voltage regulator
Loose, slipping, broken, or contaminated serpentine belt
Weak belt tensioner or overrunning alternator pulley fault
High resistance in alternator output cable, battery terminals, or grounds
Blown fuse, fusible link, sense wire, or generator control circuit problem

diagnostic_path_sections.title: Output and Belt Path
diagnostic_path_sections.summary: Confirm the alternator is driven correctly and cannot maintain voltage under load.
checks: Check alternator noise, heat, and pulley behavior

diagnostic_path_sections.title: Cable and Control Path
diagnostic_path_sections.summary: If output is inconsistent, prove the cable, ground, fuse, and control circuits before replacing the alternator.
checks: Check fusible link and charging fuse
Compare commanded and actual generator output

recommended_repairs.title: Alternator Replacement
recommended_repairs.description: Use when battery state, belt drive, cables, and command checks confirm low alternator output.

recommended_repairs.title: Serpentine Belt Replacement
recommended_repairs.description: Use when belt slip or tensioner behavior is the confirmed cause of low output.
